blocks.text: *Turn what creatures drop into the gear you want.*
Every drop is a starting point

**Every piece starts somewhere.** One kill in ten, a monster drops one piece of what it wears — an exact copy of that piece, at the **grade** and **folds** the monster wore it, with its **Ink lines** and **card slots**. An ordinary monster's gear grows with its level (Raw, then F, E and D); elites wear C and B, shadows A, and they wear more folds. Whatever it is, you can take it further: fold it with **Temper Dust** at the smith, quench it with **Quench Oil** once it reaches **+10**, write it with **Ink**, and add **card slots** at the smith. Every piece carries its own **base** — 85% to 115% of the usual — a weapon its **trademark** and an armour piece one **word** from its slot. Two drops of the same item are rarely the same, and the better one is worth more.

**Higher grades are always stronger.** Each fold adds a share of the piece's base — a small one — and a quench that succeeds adds a big one, so an **A +0** piece is worth more than eight times an **F +10** one, and every grade at +0 beats the grade below it at +10. Climbing from Raw +0 to A +10 is a long road: about two months of eight hours a day.
The four things a station does

items: **Fold** — Temper Dust and Unsigned: **1** Temper Dust a fold at Raw and one more for each grade, up to **7** at A. Each fold makes the piece worth more. **+0 to +4 always work**; from +4 a fold can fail, more often the higher the grade and the folds, and a failed fold takes **one fold off**, never below **+4**. Every grade stops at **+10**, and only a quench moves you on.

**Quench** — at **+10** only. Quench Oil and more Unsigned: **1** Quench Oil at Raw and one more for each grade, up to **6** at B. It either lifts the piece **one grade, to +0**, or fails. With no Salt, a failure drops the piece one grade, to +0 (a Raw piece just goes back to +0), and takes the last stat Ink wrote on it. **A is the top.**

**Ink** — writes one stat onto the piece at a slot you pick. An empty slot is filled; an occupied one is replaced. The Ink tab uses the strongest Ink you carry; hover the **i** beside its name to see every stat it can write with its number, a stat already in another slot greyed because it cannot land again.
**Recycle** — destroys the piece and gives back half of what its folds and quenches took, and never less than 1 Temper Dust (below).

blocks.text: **What a piece is called.** A weapon goes by the name of its trademark skill, its folds and its grade — **+7 Thousand Petals [C]**. Anything else goes by its grade, its folds and what it is — **B +6 Padded Vest**. The bag shows each piece as its picture and its card carries that title, and the bag's search finds it.

Every piece — **metal, cloth or leather** — is worked at **the smith**, and all three take the same two materials. **Temper Dust** and **Quench Oil** drop from every monster — more from higher-level monsters, far more from elites and shadows, and more again from monsters in better gear — and no shop sells them. Neither merges into anything. Every try at a station is paid for, whether it works or not, and the station's window shows the chance before you press: "Chance: 90% · If it fails: back to +4".

**Ink** comes in five tiers — Watery, Thin, Faint, Clear, Sharp — and the tier sets how big the number is. One Ink writes **one** stat, drawn from eighteen: twelve sub-stats and the six primaries, which are far rarer and worth far more. A stat already on the piece cannot roll again. There is no failure outcome: a poor roll is the failure, and the Ink is spent. **Your grade decides how many stats the piece can carry**, from none at Raw to six at A.

**Salt** comes in three — Coarse, Fine, Pure — and decides what a failed quench costs you. **Coarse Salt** keeps the grade and puts the piece at **+4**; **Fine Salt** does the same and makes the quench more likely to work; **Pure Salt** keeps the grade at **+9** and makes it more likely still. A Salt is used up whichever way the quench goes, and no quench is ever more than **95%** sure. Coarse Salt drops from ordinary monsters; Fine and Pure are rare from them and far more common from elites and shadows.
**Ten of one Ink tier merge into one of the next**, with nothing to fail. Salt merges by what it is worth: **20 Coarse** make a Fine, and **5 Fine** make a Pure. Surplus low tiers are never trash.
Recycling — half of it comes back

Take any piece to the smith and **recycle** it. The piece is destroyed, and **half of what it provably cost** comes back, as Temper Dust, Quench Oil, Unsigned and Ink: every quench it successfully climbed and the folds each of those took, the folds standing on it now, and the Ink for the stats written on it. Every fold counts, Raw ones included, and every recycle gives at least 1 Temper Dust — so a Raw piece straight from a creature gives exactly that. A shop pays 5u for any piece of gear. On the Recycle page you can tick as many carried pieces as you like and recycle them all with one press; worn pieces are recycled one at a time. A piece your first tutorial still needs cannot be recycled, sold or dropped.
**Tries that failed are not counted** — nothing anywhere remembers them — and Salt never comes back. Each material is halved on its own and rounded down, so a single unit does not survive the trip.

text: *Status: gear drops, folding, quenching, Ink, merging, recycling and weapon trademarks are all built. The costs, the odds, the Ink values and the trademark bonuses are first numbers, to be tuned in play.*
